name: Premise
short: Smartphone crowd in 140+ countries for photo, video and survey tasks; sold by contract, no public API.
summary: Premise turns a customer's questions into paid tasks in its mobile app. Contributors in over 140 countries complete them by taking photos, videos and audio recordings, answering surveys or reporting what they see at a place. Submissions go through automatic and manual quality control, and results reach the customer in a dashboard or as a raw export. It is sold for retail audits, price and market monitoring, point-of-interest mapping and verification, and situation monitoring for development and humanitarian work.

pricing.notes: No price published; the only route is Book a Demo. The SaaS Agreement bills in US dollars under an executed Order Document, with fees payable up front unless the Order Document says otherwise, auto-renewing terms (one year by default) and no refunds. Negotiated pricing is confidential. from_usd 0 means not published.

latency.typical: Same-day data once a campaign is running (company-stated).
latency.notes: The homepage says organisations 'can swiftly gather same-day data'. The 2019 brochure says a campaign 'can begin in as little as 24-48 hours' where a contributor network exists, and that recruiting and training a network in a new region takes 2-4 weeks. Contributor rejection appeals take 3-5 days.

coverage.notes: Company-stated: 'over 140 countries', '6M+ Contributors Worldwide', '25M+ Submissions per Year', '2.3M+ Unique Points of Interest', and over 120,000 traditional-trade store visits a month (December 2024). No country list or density is published. The contributor terms exclude people resident in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, Syria and Crimea. For new regions the 2019 brochure gives 2-4 weeks to recruit a network.

licensing.summary: Under the public SaaS Agreement, data 'collected specifically for Customer' under an Order Document (Collected Data) is owned by the customer, and Premise assigns 'all intellectual property rights it has' in it. Data Premise sells to other customers too (Licensed Data) comes with a non-exclusive, non-transferable, perpetual licence for internal business purposes only and 'may not be resold or otherwise directly commercialized' (the resale bar applies to Licensed Data only; Collected Data is yours). A separately negotiated master agreement overrides these terms. Contributors keep their content but grant Premise a non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable licence to exploit it for any purpose, including by the customer and the customer's clients. The terms do not name AI training by buyers, or whether Premise trains on customer data.

human.method: One account and one device per person, with no account sharing (Community Guidelines). Premise may run background and security checks at its discretion (Terms of Use), and the 2019 brochure lists account-duplication checks.
human.unknown: No identity check is required for ordinary tasks; sign-up is by Google or Apple credentials or a username and password. KYC applies only to the Premise Wallet. Contributors reach customers only as anonymous IDs, so a buyer cannot check who captured an item.

application.method: Tasks are done only in the Premise mobile app; the guidelines ban other access and 'auto' or 'macro' software. The app collects the names of installed apps so Premise can detect ones that 'doctor' location data or the clock (an installed-app scan, not attestation).
application.unknown: No device or app attestation (such as Play Integrity or App Attest) is documented.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Image Analysis in quality control checks that photos are 'not blurry or from a computer, and of the correct subject'. How screen or generated images are detected is not published. There is no C2PA or other signed capture, and Premise is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.method: Submissions carry timestamps (2019 brochure). The app checks installed apps to catch any that 'doctor' the clock.
time.unknown: Whether the timestamp comes from the device or the server, and whether the buyer receives a capture time for each item, is not documented.

location.method: The app records precise check-in and observation locations. Quality control includes location verification and machine-learning anti-spoofing. The guidelines ban mocking or spoofing location, and starting and finishing a task in different places.
location.unknown: How the coordinates are checked is undocumented, and no public proof is offered for any item.

content.method: Every submission goes through automatic (machine-learning) and manual quality control and fraud detection before it reaches the dashboard. The task brief defines the deliverable.
content.unknown: Rejection and error rates are not published.

corroboration.method: 'crowdsourced confirmation' on top of manual quality control (2019 brochure).
corroboration.unknown: Only the 2019 brochure mentions it, and current pages do not. How often items are confirmed, and by whom, is not stated.

api.notes: No public API docs. Customers use dashboards and raw data export (CSV, KMZ, PDF), and the 2019 brochure mentions a 'Data API for real-time data access' to results. api.premise.com answers most paths, including /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, with HTTP 400 'authorization header missing or malformed' (the bare root returned 200 with an empty body on 2026-10-28), so a private API exists but is undocumented (no public discovery metadata). Ordering is by sales contract; no tasking API is published.

mcp.notes: No Premise entry in the official MCP Registry (2026-10-26).

delivery.basis: 'If a network is already in place where your study is situated, your data acquisition campaign can begin in as little as 24-48 hours. For new regions, we can recruit and train a network in 2-4 weeks' (2019 brochure); 'swiftly gather same-day data' (homepage).

freshness.notes: Collected Data is captured for the customer's tasks. Licensed Data that Premise already holds is also sold, but it is not new capture.

payment.notes: No payment method is published. Fees follow an executed Order Document, are payable in US dollars at registration or renewal unless the Order Document says otherwise, are non-cancellable and non-refundable, and carry 1.5% a month on late payment.

requester.checks: No customer screening is published. Customers sign an Order Document, and the SaaS Agreement forbids unlawful use and material that violates third-party privacy. Contributors are told not to invade privacy or enter non-public spaces, and may leave any task where they feel unsafe.
requester.unknown: Whether Premise reviews task briefs, for example ones that target a specific person or private place, before contributors see them.
